title: Multi-stage Dockerfile with non-root user, /data volume, Readiness health check and container smoke script
what: Add a multi-stage Dockerfile (Maven Wrapper build stage on JDK 25, JRE 25 runtime holding only the jar), .dockerignore, a dedicated non-root user, a /data volume owned by that user with DATABASE_PATH=/data/links.db, exec-form entrypoint so the JVM is PID 1 and gets SIGTERM, and a HEALTHCHECK polling /actuator/health/readiness on the management port with a start period. Add scripts/container-test.sh that builds the image and runs it on a scratch port with a scratch volume: wait until healthy, create a Link and follow it, restart on the same volume and follow it again, check the user is not root, docker stop exits 0 within SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT + CLICK_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT plus margin with queued Clicks saved, and an invalid BASE_URL exits non-zero with a message naming BASE_URL. The script never touches port 8000 or .local/.
acceptance: `docker build .` succeeds with no local Java or Maven, and the final image contains only a JRE and the jar
`.dockerignore` excludes .local/, target/, .git and e2e/node_modules
scripts/container-test.sh passes locally: container becomes healthy, a Link is created and followed, and it is still followed after a restart on the same volume
The container process runs as a non-root user, asserted by the script
docker stop exits 0 within the graceful-shutdown bound and queued Clicks are persisted
An invalid BASE_URL makes the container exit non-zero with a message naming BASE_URL
The script uses its own port and a temporary volume and cleans up after itself
No image is pushed anywhere

title: compose.yaml for a local run with environment pass-through and a drift test
what: Add compose.yaml with one service, the /data named volume, the public port published with a configurable host port, the management port published to 127.0.0.1 only with a configurable host port, a stop_grace_period exceeding SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT + CLICK_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT, and BASE_URL, PORT, CLICK_*, SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT, LOG_FORMAT and the other settings passed from the environment with the runbook's defaults. Add a test that fails when compose.yaml passes through a setting not documented in the runbook's configuration reference, or documents one it claims to pass but doesn't, modelled on spec 0006's drift test. Validate with docker compose config.
acceptance: `docker compose up` starts the service with working defaults and it reports healthy
`BASE_URL=http://localhost:9000 PORT=9000 docker compose up` serves on that port and produces matching Short URLs
Host ports are configurable so a run never collides with 8000/8081
The management port is published only on 127.0.0.1
`docker compose down` keeps the data volume and `docker compose down -v` removes it
`docker compose config` validates in a test
The drift test fails when compose.yaml and the runbook configuration reference disagree, and passes on the committed files

title: CI: build the image and run the container tests on every pull request
what: Extend .github/workflows/ci.yml with a new, separately named job (not one of the three required check names) that builds the image and runs scripts/container-test.sh and the Compose validation on every pull request, with its own port and a temporary volume. Keep the three required job names unchanged. No registry login or push. Do not change branch protection unless the maintainer asks.
acceptance: A PR triggers the new container job, which builds the image and runs scripts/container-test.sh and the Compose test

The required checks 'Verify (format, compile, analysis, unit + integration tests)', 'Browser checks (Playwright + Lighthouse)' and 'Orchestrator (lint, types, tests)' keep their names and still run unchanged
A deliberately broken Dockerfile makes the new job fail
The workflow never pushes or deploys the image
The job uses its own port and a temporary volume

title: Docs: runbook container section, onboarding, test plan matrix, architecture, roadmap and spec index
what: Document running the container. Runbook: build, docker compose up, the /data volume and bind-mount ownership caveat, the health check, stopping and grace period, down vs down -v, and the configuration reference marked for container use. Onboarding: build and run the container and reproduce the CI container test locally. Add container rows to the matrix in docs/plans/0001-integration-testing.md. Add the container to the Mermaid diagram in docs/architecture.md. Update roadmap R11 and the spec index and status in docs/specs/README.md and the spec header.
acceptance: The runbook has a container section covering build, compose up, volume, health check, stop, down vs down -v and the bind-mount ownership note
The onboarding guide explains how to build and run the container and run the CI container test locally
The integration-testing plan matrix includes the container tests
docs/architecture.md shows the container packaging
docs/roadmap.md R11 and the docs/specs/README.md index and statuses are updated
The Compose drift test still passes against the updated runbook
